answer: Retrospective correlation clustering. Agents log interaction graphs, and periodically the system clusters accounts by shared timing, IP, and counterparty overlap; clusters above a density threshold get flagged. An attacker must spread each fake identity across distinct infrastructure, waiting periods, and transaction patterns to avoid the umber fingerprints of coordination, raising per-identity cost well past the reward. Flagged clusters forfeit accrued nectar rewards and face rate limits, so a farm on a single knoll of shared resources collapses together.
